hud-bstmy.8.6.title: Decide: required-check ruleset changes (boot jobs, Windows clippy, pixel_readback gating)
hud-bstmy.8.6.description:
Escalation (hard gate: owner account/ruleset change on GitHub 'main merge queue', ci.yml:8-11). One decision covering a single ruleset edit window.

Proposed changes:
1. Delete required jobs production-boot-vertical-slice (ci.yml:322) and canonical-app-production-boot (ci.yml:365): test-unit (ci.yml:207-211, --workspace --all-targets) already runs both tests; each recompiles the workspace and reinstalls Mesa.
2. Replace clippy-windows-gnu (ci.yml:143-180, mingw cross) with `cargo clippy --target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` inside windows.yml windows-build (native MSVC runner from T6 step 1).
3. pixel_readback: test-gpu-pixel-readback (ci.yml:580-622) is continue-on-error and gates nothing: make it blocking inside test-unit, or move it to the weekly perf lane.
vertical_slice stays (it is a required check) and the weekly perf lane stays.

Options:
A. Apply 1+2+3(blocking in test-unit); owner edits the ruleset in the same window as the PR. About -135 YAML lines, 2-3 fewer full compiles and Mesa installs per PR.
B. Apply 1+2 only; move pixel_readback to the weekly lane.
C. Status quo.

Recommendation: A (after the T8 llvmpipe recipe shows pixel_readback is stable on Mesa). Consequences: A/B require a ruleset edit or merges block on missing checks; C keeps the duplicate compile cost per PR.

Default if unanswered: C (no change to CI or the ruleset).

Line refs are at windows-release-pipeline@44d355ef (same content as main@1eb8f7cb); re-grep symbols before editing. The planning survey is not persisted; this bead is self-contained.

hud-lirh2.title: T7: Portal as a runtime feature
hud-lirh2.description:
Rebuild the text-stream portal as a runtime feature: projection state lives in the runtime keyed by PSK identity (agent_id, portal_id). Delete the external-authority design (owner tokens, audit log, provider-neutral contract, projection_authority binary, resident_grpc adapter, PortalOp channel, proto round trip, MutationProto 13-17) and fold the 12 PROJECTION_* error codes into the shared set. Internal interfaces may break; the MCP surface and the token footprint must not regress.

Governing spec: docs/scope.md 'Tranches' T7 row (target: portal code -- projection, driver, windowed portal, composer -- under ~12k lines from ~43k); docs/api.md 'MCP tools' (portal verbs), 'Errors', 'Design decisions (T5)' item 4; docs/invariants.md §2, §3, §4, §5, §8, §9.

Regression guard: the POC headless acceptance portal tests (poc_portal_attach_stream_reply_detach, poc_portal_abandoned_is_reclaimed) must land before T7 starts and stay green throughout.

## Success Criteria
1. PortalHub keyed by (agent_id, portal_id) is the only portal state; no owner tokens, PortalOp channel, audit log, contract, coalescer, projection_authority bin or resident_grpc adapter remain.
2. PROJECTION_* codes are gone from the shared error set; portal rejections map to shared codes with hints.
3. MutationProto 13-17 are reserved; the driver calls scene methods directly.
4. The four portal groups total <= ~12k lines (measured, recorded in scope.md).
5. token_footprint gate byte-identical; POC headless portal tests green; invariant test lists updated.
6. Owner Windows check of the portal (rendering, typing, liveness, drag/resize, dismiss) passes.
hud-lirh2.design:

Cohesion override: 13 children because the migration must keep `just ci` green at every step; each step is an independently revertible PR on a 43k-line surface.
Decisions (coordinator 2026-10-03): token-footprint bytes stay identical (keep `canonical-input-0001` via a test hook, no baseline re-approval); D1 portal `key` always replaces the newest unit with that key; D2 delete the gRPC raw-tile composer path; portals keyed by (agent_id, portal_id), a second agent using the same portal id gets its own portal. dependencies.title: Global safe-mode hotkey and windowed safe-mode overlay
dependencies.description:
Goal: a human can enter and exit safe mode on the unfocused, click-through overlay with a global hotkey (default Ctrl+Shift+F12, configurable), and the windowed path draws the safe-mode chrome while active.
